payload.task_text:
You are a course analytics assistant for the Foundations of Finance course offered in Fall 2013. This course has a course ID of 16 in the learning management system.

Your task has three parts.

Part 1: Retrieve all assignments for course 16 and gather submission statistics for each one. For each assignment, collect the assignment name, total number of submissions, average score (rounded to 2 decimal places), number of late submissions, and late submission rate (late submissions divided by total submissions, multiplied by 100, rounded to 2 decimal places).

Part 2: Create a Google Forms survey titled "Foundations of Finance - Assignment Feedback Survey" to collect student feedback on assignments. The survey must contain exactly 5 questions covering the following topics: overall assignment workload, clarity of assignment instructions, time required to complete assignments, availability of instructor support, and overall satisfaction with the assignments. Use appropriate question types for each.

Part 3: Create a Word document called Assignment_Analysis.docx in the workspace. The document must have the title "Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013) - Assignment Analysis" at the top. It must contain a table with the following columns in this exact order: Assignment_Name, Total_Submissions, Avg_Score, Late_Submissions, Late_Rate(%). Sort the rows alphabetically by Assignment_Name. Include all assignments found in the course that have at least one submission (assignments with no submissions may be excluded).

After creating the Word document, send a summary email to instructor@financeou.example.com from analytics@university.example.com with the subject "Assignment Analysis Report - Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013)". The email body must mention the total number of assignments analyzed, the assignment with the highest average score, and the assignment with the most late submissions. Also include the Google Forms survey link in the email body.

The initial workspace contains Assignment_Guidelines.pdf for reference on the grading criteria used in this course.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently,

This is a compact one-course task. The main agent completes it directly; do not dispatch any sub-agent. Canvas is read-only.

First resolve the task-visible workspace directory from the runtime allowed-directory listing (or the literal accessible-workspace directory already supplied by the harness), freeze it as `<workspace_root>`, and reject bare `/workspace` and dumps/run-specific paths. In one native-parallel response, call `canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true)`, extract all pages of `<workspace_root>/Assignment_Guidelines.pdf` read-only with `python_execute`, call `create_form(title="Foundations of Finance - Assignment Feedback Survey")` exactly once, and search Sent mail for the exact recipient/subject. Select exactly one returned course whose code is `FFF-2013J` and whose full name is `Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013)`; stop on zero or multiple matches, and never retry Form creation after an ambiguous result. Then call `canvas_list_assignments(course_id=<literal returned course ID>)` once.

From the returned assignment list, issue one independent `canvas_list_assignment_submissions(course_id=<literal returned course ID>, assignment_id=<returned assignment ID>, page=1, per_page=1)` call per assignment in one native-parallel response. Use the whole-assignment `summary` returned on each call; do not page raw submissions. For every assignment with `summary.total_count>0`, compute:
`Total_Submissions=total_count`, `Avg_Score=round(avg_score,2)`, `Late_Submissions=late_count`, and `Late_Rate(%)=round(100*late_count/total_count,2)`.
Sort rows by exact assignment name. Select highest average score and most late submissions with assignment-name ascending tie-breaks.

Freeze one literal canonical payload containing all sorted rows, analyzed count, the two named extrema, and the verified Form ID/responder link. The Word document and email must consume exactly this payload without recomputing statistics.

Complete the Form chain on the retained ID, adding exactly these five multiple-choice questions in order and then reading the Form back:
1. `How would you rate the overall assignment workload?` — `Very light, Light, About right, Heavy, Very heavy`
2. `How clear were the assignment instructions?` — `Very unclear, Unclear, Neutral, Clear, Very clear`
3. `How much time did you typically spend on each assignment?` — `Less than 1 hour, 1-3 hours, 4-6 hours, 7-10 hours, More than 10 hours`
4. `How available was instructor support for assignments?` — `Never available, Rarely available, Sometimes available, Usually available, Always available`
5. `What is your overall satisfaction with the assignments?` — `1, 2, 3, 4, 5`
Require exactly this five-question sequence on the newly retained Form ID; do not append duplicates.

Create `<workspace_root>/Assignment_Analysis.docx` exactly once, preferably atomically with `python-docx`, using title `Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013) - Assignment Analysis` and one table with exact columns `Assignment_Name, Total_Submissions, Avg_Score, Late_Submissions, Late_Rate(%)`. Read the document back and require every canonical row in alphabetical order with literal numeric values.

For email idempotency, paginate `search_emails(query="Assignment Analysis Report - Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013)", folder="Sent", page=<n>, page_size=50)`, read every candidate, and match complete To, From, and Subject. Send exactly once only when no exact match exists, from `analytics@university.example.com` to `instructor@financeou.example.com`. The body must include canonical analyzed count, named highest-average assignment, named most-late assignment, and verified Form responder link. Repeat search/read-back and require exactly one exact message.

Accept only after the Form, Word file, and email read back against the same canonical payload.

nodes.text:
You are helping with course analytics for the "Foundations of Finance" course (Fall 2013), which has Canvas course ID 16.

TASK: Retrieve ALL assignments for course 16 and gather submission statistics for EACH assignment. 

For every assignment in the course, collect and report:
1. Assignment name
2. Assignment ID
3. Total number of submissions (count of students who submitted; use the summary totals returned by the submissions endpoint)
4. Average score (mean of submitted scores), rounded to 2 decimal places
5. Number of late submissions (submissions marked late)
6. Late submission rate = (late submissions / total submissions) * 100, rounded to 2 decimal places

STEPS:
- Use mcp__canvas__canvas_list_assignments with course_id=16 to get all assignments (include unpublished if present).
- For each assignment, use mcp__canvas__canvas_list_assignment_submissions with course_id=16 and the assignment_id to get submissions and the summary totals (it returns summary totals covering the whole assignment). If pagination is needed (pagination.has_more), page through with per_page=100 until done.
- Handle assignments with ZERO submissions correctly: total submissions = 0, average score = 0 (or "N/A" — but prefer reporting 0.00), late submissions = 0, late rate = 0.00. Clearly flag which assignments have zero submissions.

OUTPUT FORMAT: Return a structured list, one entry per assignment, in this exact format:
- Assignment Name: <name>
- Assignment ID: <id>
- Total Submissions: <n>
- Avg Score: <x.xx>
- Late Submissions: <n>
- Late Rate(%): <x.xx>
- Has Submissions: yes/no

Then provide a final summary line: "TOTAL_ASSIGNMENTS: <count>" and "ASSIGNMENTS_WITH_SUBMISSIONS: <count>". Be precise with the numbers — they will be used verbatim to build a report and email. Do not modify any data (read-only task).
Gather Canvas assignment stats

You are creating a Google Forms survey for student feedback on course assignments.

TASK: Create a Google Form with the EXACT title "Foundations of Finance - Assignment Feedback Survey". The survey must contain EXACTLY 5 questions covering these topics, using appropriate question types:

1. "Overall assignment workload" — use a multiple choice question with options: ["Very Light", "Light", "Moderate", "Heavy", "Very Heavy"]
2. "Clarity of assignment instructions" — use a multiple choice question with options: ["Very Unclear", "Unclear", "Neutral", "Clear", "Very Clear"]
3. "Time required to complete assignments" — use a multiple choice question with options: ["Less than 1 hour", "1-3 hours", "3-5 hours", "More than 5 hours"]
4. "Availability of instructor support" — use a multiple choice question with options: ["Very Poor", "Poor", "Fair", "Good", "Excellent"]
5. "Overall satisfaction with the assignments" — use a multiple choice question with options: ["Very Dissatisfied", "Dissatisfied", "Neutral", "Satisfied", "Very Satisfied"]

Use the Google Forms tools: mcp__google_forms__create_form (title), then mcp__google_forms__add_multiple_choice_question for each of the 5 questions with the options listed above.

After creating, call mcp__google_forms__get_form with the formId to retrieve form details.

OUTPUT: Report back:
- The form ID
- The survey share link (the form's responder/view URL, e.g. https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/<ID>/viewform — derive it from the form details returned by get_form if a link is provided; otherwise construct the standard public viewform URL from the formId)
- Confirmation that all 5 questions were added (list the question titles in order).

Do NOT add any extra questions beyond the 5 specified. Do not modify anything else.
Create Google Forms feedback survey

You are building a Word document report for the "Foundations of Finance" course (Fall 2013) using the local Word tools (mcp__word__*).

The document must contain:
1. A title at the top (use a Heading 1 or large title paragraph): "Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013) - Assignment Analysis"
2. A table with these EXACT column headers in this exact order: Assignment_Name | Total_Submissions | Avg_Score | Late_Submissions | Late_Rate(%)
3. Rows for exactly these 12 assignments (already sorted alphabetically by Assignment_Name — use this order):

CMA 34878 | 1470 | 83.32 | 36 | 2.45
CMA 34879 | 1352 | 87.97 | 43 | 3.18
CMA 34880 | 1252 | 76.50 | 61 | 4.87
CMA 34881 | 1224 | 78.30 | 59 | 4.82
CMA 34882 | 1193 | 78.65 | 75 | 6.29
CMA 34883 | 1196 | 76.80 | 119 | 9.95
CMA 34884 | 1160 | 76.16 | 88 | 7.59
TMA 34873 | 1859 | 78.16 | 157 | 8.45
TMA 34874 | 1661 | 72.45 | 193 | 11.62
TMA 34875 | 1402 | 70.49 | 376 | 26.82
TMA 34876 | 1313 | 71.05 | 268 | 20.41
TMA 34877 | 1158 | 75.89 | 148 | 12.78

Note: The table has 1 header row + 12 data rows = 13 rows, 5 columns. Enter the values EXACTLY as given (e.g., "CMA 34878", "1470", "83.32", "36", "2.45"). The header row must use the exact header names with underscores as specified.

Steps:
- Use mcp__word__create_document with filename = the full path above.
- Use mcp__word__add_heading (level 1) or add_paragraph for the title text "Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013) - Assignment Analysis".
- Use mcp__word__add_table with rows=13, cols=5, and data = 2D array where row 0 is the header and rows 1-12 are the data rows above (in the given order).
- Optionally format the header row (e.g., bold) with mcp__word__format_table_cell_text or highlight_table_header — keep it simple and correct.
- Verify by reading back the document text (mcp__word__get_document_text) and confirm the title and all 12 rows with correct values are present.

DELIVERABLE: Confirm the file was created at the exact path, the title is present, the header row matches exactly, and all 12 data rows match the values above. Report the final file path.
Create Assignment_Analysis.docx

You are sending a summary email using the email tools (mcp__emails__*).

TASK: Send ONE email with the following exact parameters:
- To: instructor@financeou.example.com
- From: analytics@university.example.com (use the from_addr parameter; if the tool does not accept from_addr, use the mailbox default identity)
- Subject: "Assignment Analysis Report - Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013)"

Body (plain text) must mention ALL of the following:
1. Total number of assignments analyzed: 12
2. The assignment with the highest average score: CMA 34879 (average score 87.97)
3. The assignment with the most late submissions: TMA 34875 (376 late submissions)
4. The Google Forms survey link: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/99880271-00e9-4851-997f-af00c0eadfa7/viewform

Suggested body text (write it in a professional tone, covering all four points above):

"Hello,

Please find the assignment analysis summary for the Foundations of Finance course (Fall 2013).

Total number of assignments analyzed: 12
Assignment with the highest average score: CMA 34879 (average score 87.97)
Assignment with the most late submissions: TMA 34875 (376 late submissions)

The student feedback survey for assignments is available here: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/99880271-00e9-4851-997f-af00c0eadfa7/viewform

Course Analytics Team"

Use mcp__emails__send_email. After sending, confirm the email was sent successfully and report the recipient, subject, and sender.
